rationale: This is a near-cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "Positive R&D Workforce Scaling" (same indicator, same two ingredients, only the R&D term recentered), and the zero-masked contracting firms are dumped into the middle of the centered distribution, so the "genuine comparison" claim is undermined by an uninterpretable mass at zero rather than by a new economic mechanism.

Replacing the inverse-investment denominator of "Positive Dual-Capital Payoff" with a centered R&D-share-of-investment mix is a substantive fix to the sign conflict rather than a cosmetic tweak, though the signal still lumps all non-growers at exactly zero in the middle of the score distribution and the R&D/(capx+R&D) mix is close to the well-documented R&D-versus-tangible-investment tilt.

Stripped of the intensity weight, this is essentially the long-known R&D-to-capex composition premium (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis and the tangible-investment/asset-growth anomalies) combined multiplicatively with an investment-intensity rank that is itself the classic negative investment effect, so it is a rediscovery of two published anomalies rather than a novel cross-theme interaction.

The "acquired stock versus organic reinvestment flow" framing is economically distinct from the acquirer-underperformance and goodwill-impairment literatures and the expression matches the stated sign, but COALESCE(gdwl,0) puts a large block of never-acquiring firms at exactly zero, so the long leg risks being a zero-goodwill dummy rather than a low-ratio portfolio.

The expected sign is flipped purely to fit one prior in-sample result (ls_alpha 0.023 with an expectation of negative), and the triple MIN combines three highly correlated characteristics — R&D intensity and cash holdings, both of which carry their own published premia — so a positive result would be hard to attribute to the stated optionality mechanism.

Debt-maturity structure conditioned on R&D intensity is a coherent rollover-risk mechanism that is genuinely distinct from the archived debt-issuance signal and the expression's direction matches the negative expected sign, though dlc/(dltt+dlc) is unstable for the near-zero-debt firms that dominate the high-R&D leg and coverage should be checked carefully.
